clue.text: Creature appearing briefly in St Augustine's diocese?

definitions.text: Creature appearing briefly in St Augustine's diocese?

parts.words: Creature appearing briefly in St Augustine's diocese?
parts.note: St Augustine was bishop of Hippo in North Africa, and a big river animal shortened to its everyday clipped form gives that same see's name

explanation.surface: A question about some animal glimpsed for a moment in a saint's diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appearing briefly' means the creature's name is cut short: the clipped form is HIPPO, the North African city where St Augustine was bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the large African river mammal whose clipped nickname matches Augustine's bishopric.

clue.text: Master speedily beginning, to resuscitate pet?

annotationWithheld.why: Master speedily beginning, to resuscitate pet? (7): an anagram of MASTER needs an extra H, and no clue word ('speedily beginning' gives S) supplies it
annotationWithheld.clue: Master speedily beginning, to resuscitate pet?

clue.text: In a city in France he serves an Eastern dish

indicators.note: the word In tells us one piece sits inside the other piece here

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
il is the French word for he

explanation.surface: A waiter in a French city brings out an Oriental meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container; the French city and the French pronoun are the convention here, and 'serves' is only a link to the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is spiced rice cooked in stock, a dish from the Middle East and South Asia.

clue.text: Frank is said to support striking

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
something said is spoken

explanation.surface: Frank is reported to back the strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the definition. In a down clue 'to support' puts SPOKEN under OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frank speaks bluntly and openly, without holding back.

clue.text: Instrument almost obtained with pound coin once

indicators.note: almost means the woodwind word loses its final letter here

parts.note: an oboe is a woodwind instrument
L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Somebody nearly got hold of an instrument plus a pound coin from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts OBOE to OBO; add L for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece.

clue.text: A Greek character always attaining success

definitions.note: a verb phrase here, standing for a person who attains success

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A Greek man who never fails to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person, but it is the letter CHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reaches goals and wins success is called an achiever.

clue.text: Like the situation of an 11th-century bishop of Rome?

definitions.text: Like the situation of an 11th-century bishop of Rome?

parts.words: Like the situation of an 11th-century bishop of Rome?
parts.note: Pope ... II reigned in the eleventh century, and a pope's situation is in a city, so his name also describes town life

explanation.surface: A question about where a medieval pope was based.
explanation.walkthrough: Urban II was pope from 1088 to 1099, and a bishop of Rome lives in a city, so the pope's name is also an adjective for a city setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The pope's name doubles as the adjective for a setting in a town or city.

clue.text: Part made by soldiers replacing one in invention

indicators.note: replacing means one piece is swapped out of the word for invention and another put in its place

parts.note: a figment is something invented, as in a figment of the imagination
I is the Roman numeral for one
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Something partly built by troops who took over from one inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Artillery) takes the place of I (one) in FIGMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a broken-off piece, a small portion of something whole.

clue.text: Like some music for the church — not written down

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: Church music that is handed on by ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music sung by a choir.

clue.text: One arriving early with the first lot of champers

definitions.text: One arriving early with the first lot of champers

parts.words: One arriving early with the first lot of champers
parts.note: champers is slang for champagne, but here it means teeth, things that champ; the first lot comes in a baby's mouth

explanation.surface: Someone who turns up early just as the first bottles of fizz are opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champers' is British slang for champagne, which sets up a party; here it means the teeth that champ, and the first set arrives early in childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's first set of teeth come through in infancy and later fall out.

clue.text: Some can still remember this situation

indicators.note: Some means only part of the following words is taken, the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some people can still recall this position.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'rememBER THis'.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a job or post, as in a comfortable berth in the civil service.

clue.text: It would be very helpful of you if you turned up these ruffs

definitions.text: It would be very helpful of you if you turned up these
definitions.meaning: to turn up with the winning cards is an idiom for being unexpectedly helpful
in card games to ruff is to play a winning-suit card on a led suit

explanation.surface: A request phrased as a compliment, dressed up with Elizabethan collars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up trumps' means to come through usefully; 'ruffs' looks like frilly collars but is the bridge verb for playing a trump.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist, a player ruffs by playing a card of the winning suit, which is what the plural also names.

clue.text: Generate trouble for one not necessarily in the minority

definitions.text: one not necessarily in the minority

indicators.note: trouble works as a verb here, meaning the word Generate is stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble for someone who is not part of a small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' suggests a small group, but means being a minor, under 18: a person aged 18 or 19 is still in this group but is an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen; the last two years of that span are past legal minority, hence 'not necessarily'.

clue.text: Retired King to live outside our country and lecture

indicators.note: Retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the royal abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina; R alone is rex, and here the king/queen cipher ER is used

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
for a British paper, our country is the UK

explanation.surface: A king in retirement goes to live abroad and gives a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the royal cipher round to give RE; 'outside' wraps BE round UK. 'And' is a link word, and 'lecture' means scold, not a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone can mean to scold them sternly, the same as a reprimand.

clue.text: Jazz fan's lines about Bo-peep's misfortune

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is a noun phrase linked to the wordplay

indicators.note: about means the lines go around the rest

parts.note: BR is British Rail, a railway system of lines

indicators.note: misfortune signals that the nursery rhyme name is upset and its letters scrambled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A jazz fan sings of the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misfortune' makes EBOPPE from the nursery-rhyme name, and 'about' puts BR (British Rail) round it; the 's of the definition is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast 1940s jazz style, and a follower of it is a bebopper.

clue.text: Main weapon found at the coast

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a thing found on the coast

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main
a shell is an explosive artillery round

explanation.surface: A gun or bomb washed up on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but is the poetic noun for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty mollusc cases wash up on beaches and are collected there.

clue.text: Sprinter's first trainer defending vulgar laggard

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Sprinter's is used

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar
a coach trains athletes

explanation.surface: An athlete's coach sticks up for a crude slowpoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes S from Sprinter's, which looks like the definition's subject but only gives a letter; 'defending' puts COACH round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dawdles and falls behind the rest is a slowcoach.

clue.text: Energetic person given sack and shot!

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a ball is a shot, as in an old cannonball

explanation.surface: A lively person is dismissed and then shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireball is a person of fierce drive and energy.

clue.text: Dashing girl coming out and broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a girl making her debut in high society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A lively young woman makes her debut and goes on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' is a debutante's first season in society; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair person has a confident, stylish charm.

clue.text: Restraint of the French engineers on board

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
RE is the Royal Engineers
SS stands for steamship, so being on board is being on an SS

explanation.surface: French engineers on a ship are held back.
explanation.walkthrough: DU (French 'of the'), RE (Royal Engineers), SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is constraint or compulsion by threat or force.

clue.text: Literary character who wove a bed?

definitions.meaning: Nick the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream is given an ass's head
the bed of a river or sea is its floor

explanation.surface: A weaver from a book made himself a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word; 'bed' is a river bed, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's weaver bears this name, and a seabed is the lowest floor of the sea.

clue.text: Building-work thus skirted by island transport system

indicators.note: skirted by means surrounded at the edges by the island word

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
so means thus, in this way
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Construction is ringed by an island's railway network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirted by' has the Isle of Man, a British island, wrap SO; the railway abbreviation then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is stone or brick construction built by a mason.

clue.text: Go to drivers' place without a single witty retort

indicators.note: without means the single letter is taken away from the other piece

parts.note: to repair to a place is to go there
I is the Roman numeral for one
golf drivers hit the ball from the tee

explanation.surface: Head to the golf tee without a quip ready.
explanation.walkthrough: REPAIR less I gives REPAR; 'drivers' are golf clubs, not motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, clever conversation of witty replies.

clue.text: Raced chestnut from farm

parts.note: raced means ran
CH is the abbreviation for chestnut, the horse colour

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse sped away from the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle in America.

clue.text: Attack in the drive, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an ... is an old word for a sudden fit or bout, as in an ... of rage
a driveway is an example of a way in

explanation.surface: An assault on a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure of temper is an old meaning, and the way you enter a property is the other.

clue.text: Radical youth leader replacing end of girl's article

indicators.note: replacing means one letter in the girl's name is taken out and another put in

parts.note: Ethel is a girl's name

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of youth is used

explanation.surface: A radical young leader changes the end of a girl's piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: ETHEL contains THE, an article; 'end of' it is its E, which Y (the 'leader' of youth) replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit, and ethyl is one.

clue.text: Guy seen around East End, for example

indicators.note: around means one piece goes about the other

parts.note: say means for example

indicators.note: End means only the last letter of East is used

explanation.surface: A man spotted near London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a district of London, but 'East End' here is just the T at the end of East, which goes inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope that steadies a tent or mast, and so is a stay.

clue.text: Writer out east with a forbidding appearance

indicators.note: out means that the compass letter is removed

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A grim-looking author is out in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: STERNE loses E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern face looks severe and strict.

clue.text: Cunning schemes backed by a ruler in a foreign city

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other
backed means the word for wiles is read in reverse

parts.note: arts are wiles or cunning schemes
a khan is a ruler in central Asia

explanation.surface: Cunning plots supported by a monarch in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns ARTS to STRA; 'by' sets it beside A KHAN, with the A placed first. Astrakhan, on the Volga, is also a curly lambswool fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a city on the Volga delta in Russia.

clue.text: Hesitate to mention a scatty girl without aspirations

annotationWithheld.why: Hesitate to mention a scatty girl without aspirations (6-6): SILLY and SALLY each take an H outside, but the one indicator 'without' must serve both containers, which the check refuses as a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Hesitate to mention a scatty girl without aspirations
